_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Sonobuoy Monthly Status Report
summary: Documents the status of the contractor effort toward achieving contract objectives, including accomplishments, difficulties encountered, and progress compared to planned goals, used by the Government to monitor and evaluate contractor performance.
use_relationship:
The Sonobuoy Monthly Status Report documents the status of the contractor effort towards achieving contract objectives. It identifies accomplishments to date and difficulties encountered, and compares the status achieved to planned goals and the resources expended. It is used by the Government to monitor and evaluate contractor performance.

This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format and content, and intended use information for the data deliverable resulting from the work task described in the contract.

This DID supersedes DI-SESS-82320.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The format for the report shall be any combination of the following: Microsoft (MS) Power Point Presentation, MS Excel, or MS Word and shall include graphics as required.

children.title: The content for the Sonobuoy Monthly Status Report shall be as follows
Materials
Obsolete and potentially obsolete parts status
Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS)
Material, Supplier, Critical Supplier Changes
Supplier Site Visit Schedule
Supplier Management & Supplier Quality
children.content: See Figure 1 for additional guidance.

children.title: Production and Contractor Data Requirements List (CDRL) contract and actual delivery schedules to include
children.content: Contract number, nomenclature of the system or program, and period covered by the report.

children.title: Summary of recent testing
children.content: (sample lot, Engineering Change Proposal [ECP] or qualification), test results, and failure analysis.

children.title: Risk Matrix with risk description, impact, response and actions
children.content: Shall be included.

children.title: Status of engineering test units provided as part of the contract
children.content: With brief summary of results/failures.

children.title: A list and summary of ECP status, including identification of proposed ECPs, approved ECPs, and implemented ECPs to include the following
children.content: Contract and buoy type, description of change, level of change, purpose of change, lot number and date that ECP changes were implemented into production.

children.title: Any significant changes to the contractor's organization or method of operation
children.content: To the project management network, to the production line layout, or to the milestone charts.

children.title: Problem areas affecting technical, scheduling or cost elements of the programs
children.content: With background, and any recommendations for solutions beyond the scope of the contract.

children.title: Plans of activities during the following reporting period
children.content: To include meeting schedule and certification event.

children.title: Quality
Quality metrics that are documented and tracked in support of the Contractor's Quality Management System (QMS)
children.content: To include metrics and findings associated with scrap, repair, rework, first pass yield, lot acceptance test results/failures, Engineering Test Article results/failures, FIAR investigation results; and the root cause and corrective actions (RCCA) taken to mitigate and preclude their reoccurrence.

children.title: Continuous Process Improvements
Internal AS9100 schedule chart
Listing of all open and new events for the current monthly reporting period, by buoy type, with a brief description, including remaining actions to closure, of the following
List of Company internal Class II Engineering Change Notices (ECN)
Nonconforming Material Reports (NMCR/QIR)
Corrective & Preventive Action Requests (CAR/CAPA)
Requests for Variance
Internal failures due to Calibration
Fill out Figure 2 "Delta PRR Content" on a monthly basis
children.content: And provide briefing material associated with the areas that were identified as having changed.

children.title: Sonobuoy Defect Waterfall Charts
children.content: The Sonobuoy Defect Waterfall Chart provides a concise, visual reference of current and historical Lot Acceptance Test results. It provides information for each Production Lot with regard to manufacturing completion date, samples testing location and date, # of samples tested, # of defects recorded, PASS/FAIL status, and description of the defects observed. A separate chart must be maintained for each buoy type, and must be included as slides in the Monthly Production Status Report CDRL A00A. In addition, the updated Excel files are to be submitted for each buoy type along with the Monthly Production Status Report. Instructions for building and maintaining the spreadsheets are provided below. Table 1 provides a visual reference of the spreadsheet. Example data is included in the Table for clarity.

children.title: Reference Document(s)
children.content: N/A

children.title: Format
children.content: The Chart shall be in Microsoft Excel format, Arial 10 or 11-point font. Cells should be set to wrap. Cells should be formatted per the Table below, i.e., Date formatting, Text, and Number field formats. All number fields should be numeric, with zero (0) decimal places. Fields including alphanumeric information should be Text formatted. Columns of PASS Lots should be highlighted Green. Columns of FAILED Lots should be highlighted light red.

children.title: Content
Row 1 should provide the Chart Title "Defect Waterfall Chart"
children.content: Including buoy type, manufacturer name, Contract #, and Submittal Date.

children.title: Rows 2-14 should be titled in column B as shown in Table 1
children.content: With appropriate data provided beginning in column C. The manufacturer shall supply the information requested in Rows 2-6. The information in Rows 7-10, 12, and 14 can be found in the Acceptance Test Report (ATR) provided by the Government following each Lot Acceptance Test. These reports are submitted to the manufacturer typically within two business days following the test. Rows 11 and 13 (Cumulative Totals of Major and Minor Defects) shall be calculated.

children.title: Rows 15 and 16 form the transition to display of Defects observed during the Lot Acceptance Testing
children.content: Row 16 is the Header for the Major Defects to be recorded below.

children.title: The actual Defect Codes to be recorded in the Chart
children.content: Can be found in the ATR submitted by the Government following each Lot Acceptance Test. Enter the Code in column A and the Description in column B. Only the Defects observed should be listed on the Chart. The list will grow as the number of tests displayed (i.e., # of columns) increases. Add or insert Rows as necessary, while maintaining the Defect Codes listed in proper alphanumeric sort order (per the Code in column A).

children.title: Below the section for Major Defects is a section for Minor Defects
children.content: This should be maintained in similar fashion to 3.12.3.4.

children.title: General Instruction
Manufacturer should use judgement regarding the number of columns displayed on the slides in the Monthly Report
children.content: More than 15 columns of data in Landscape format will become difficult to read. Add Slides as necessary to cover the desired amount of historical data. Typically, the current and prior Government Fiscal Years (GFY) is sufficient.

children.title: Freezing columns A and B will allow data columns to be hidden if necessary
children.content: When preparing snapshot slides for reporting.

children.title: Each buoy type Excel file should segregate the data using individual tabs for each GFY
children.content: A Chart/Tab should only include data from Lots of a single Contract Year. Contract Year Lots are as specified in the Contract by year, i.e., the year of Lot Purchases. They are NOT related to the actual date of manufacture and/or testing.

children.title: Lot # nomenclature shall include appropriate indication
children.content: If a Lot was previously withdrawn from testing (e.g., Lot 9(W)) or if Samples were submitted for testing a second or a third time (e.g., Lot 9(2), 9(3)).

children.title: Lot # columns shall be ordered chronologically by Lot Acceptance Test Date
